(a) City's right of oversight. The work of constructing, erecting and maintaining facilities of a telephone company shall be done under the regulation of the city and shall be subject to the police power of the city and the city's ordinances. The city has the right to oversee, regulate and inspect the installation, construction, technical operation, upgrade, repair, maintenance and removal of equipment in accordance with the provisions of this division and applicable law. The city reserves the right to adopt or issue such rules, regulations, orders or other directives governing a telephone company or its equipment as it shall find necessary or appropriate in the exercise of its police power or the management of the city streets and such other orders as the city shall find necessary or appropriate pursuant to and in furtherance of the purposes of this division. The use of the streets by a telephone company shall not interfere with the use of the streets by others except to the extent permitted by this division. The telephone company shall leave all streets and other property in as good condition as that prevailing prior to the telephone company's installation, construction, technical operation, upgrade, repair, maintenance or removal of the equipment from the streets and without materially affecting, altering or disturbing in any way any electric or other cables or wires or any pipes, structures or attachments. The city shall have the right to inspect and approve the condition of such streets and to require the telephone company to make any additional repairs in order to bring such streets to the condition required by this division.
(b) Regulation of use of streets preserved. Nothing in this division restricts the authority of the city to regulate the use and occupancy of the streets by any person or entity providing service. Persons or entities subject to paying a fee pursuant to chapter 14, article II, division 2 shall not be exempt from municipal regulations relating to the time, manner and method of installation, construction, technical operation, upgrade, repair, maintenance and removal of the equipment located within the city's streets. Pursuant to applicable provisions of the city charter and other general law, the city expressly reserves its right to require a franchise from any telephone company providing service whose equipment occupies the city's streets.
(c) Permits and approvals. Pursuant to city ordinances or other applicable regulations, a telephone company shall obtain all construction, building or other permits or approvals necessary before constructing, installing, operating, upgrading, repairing, maintaining or removing equipment. Prior to the city's issuing a construction, building or other permit, a telephone company may be required to:
(1) Submit an application in writing specifically describing the nature, extent and location of the portion of the rights-of-way to be used by the telephone company; and
(2) Furnish an indemnity bond acceptable to the city or other security acceptable to the city for any damage to any part of the street, the city or to any member of the public caused by the work of the telephone company performed under authority of such permit.
The obligations of the telephone company under this division and any liability of the telephone company shall not be limited by the city's acceptance of the bond or the security. Any fees that the city charges to a telephone company to issue construction, building or other permits or approvals shall not be offset against the compensation that a telephone company is required to pay to the city pursuant to chapter 14, article II, division 2 nor against any other fees or taxes the telephone company may pay the city.
(d) Repair and replacement of streets. A telephone company shall, at its own cost and expense, replace and properly relay and repair the surface, base and landscape treatment of any public sidewalk or street that may be excavated or damaged by reason of the erection, construction, maintenance or repair of its facilities promptly and in no event later than ten days after completion of the work in accordance with existing standards of the city in effect at the time of the work. Upon failure of a telephone company to perform any such repair or replacement, after ten days' notice from the city, the city or its agent or contractor may repair such portion of the streets as may have been disturbed by a telephone company, its contractors or agents and, upon receipt of a bill from the city, a telephone company will promptly reimburse the city for its costs so incurred. Such repair or replacement shall restore the streets to the condition required by subsection (a) of this section.
(e) Abandoned equipment. All equipment including both aerial and underground equipment that is abandoned within the public rights-of-way shall be removed by the telephone company unless an alternative plan is approved by the city. Any abandoned equipment allowed to remain in the public rights-of-way shall continue to be the responsibility of the telephone company. Such telephone company shall be liable for all costs and damages arising from the presence of the abandoned equipment in the public rights-of-way.
(f) New grades or lines; relocations. If the grades or lines of any street are changed at any time during the term, then the telephone company shall, at its own cost and expense and upon the notice of the city, protect or promptly alter or relocate equipment so as to conform with such new grades or lines. Upon notice from the city, a telephone company shall remove and relocate equipment where the city deems such removal and relocation necessary as a result of the construction or maintenance of any part of the street or due to the extension of a public road. If a telephone company refuses or neglects to so protect, alter or relocate equipment, in accordance with this subsection, the city shall have the right to break through, remove, alter or relocate such equipment and a telephone company shall pay to the city the costs incurred in connection with such breaking through, removal, alteration or relocation. The city and its officers, employees, agents, attorneys, consultants and independent contractors shall not have any liability to the telephone company for any damage as a result of or in connection with the breaking through, removal, alteration or relocation.
(g) Quality. All work involved in the installation, construction, technical operation, upgrade, repair, maintenance and removal of equipment shall be performed in a safe, thorough and reliable manner using materials of good and durable quality. If, at any time, it is determined by the city or any other agency or authority of competent jurisdiction that any equipment is harmful to the health or safety of any person, then a telephone company shall, at its own cost and expense, promptly correct all such conditions.
(h) No obstruction. In connection with the installation, construction, technical operation, upgrade, repair, maintenance and removal of equipment, a telephone company shall not obstruct the streets, subways, railways, rivers or other traffic to, from or within the corporate limits of the city without the prior consent of the city. Equipment of a telephone company in the streets shall be located so as to cause minimum interference with the use of the streets and adjoining property.
(i) No interference. A telephone company shall not interfere with the technical operation of any other telecommunications system or any other utility operating within the rights-of-way within the corporate limits of the city.
(j) Underground utilities. A telephone company shall comply with any current or future city ordinances, rules or orders requiring the placement of equipment underground.
(k) Moving equipment. A telephone company shall, upon prior written notice by the city or any person holding a permit to move any structure and, within the time that is reasonable under the circumstances, temporarily move equipment to permit the moving of said structure. A telephone company may impose a reasonable charge on any person other than the city for any such movement of its equipment.
(l) Emergency relocation of equipment. The city may, at any time, in case of fire, disaster or other emergency as determined by the city in its sole discretion, cut or move equipment, in which event the city shall not incur any liability to a telephone company, any affiliated person or any other person. When possible, a telephone company shall be consulted prior to any such cutting or movement of equipment and shall be given the opportunity to perform such work itself. All costs to repair or replace such equipment shall be borne by a telephone company. If the city determines that the failure of a telephone company to properly restore or repair the streets constitutes a safety hazard to the public, the city may undertake emergency repairs and restoration efforts. A telephone company shall promptly reimburse the city for all costs incurred by the city in regard to the repair or restoration.
(m) Street closings. If all or any part of the streets are eliminated, discontinued or de-mapped, the telephone company shall cease operation of the telecommunications system with respect to such streets upon the effective date of a final action of the city in connection therewith.

(a) The city council finds that it should maintain broad jurisdiction over the regulation of subdivisions. Whenever property is divided, the public interest is affected to a degree. Property lines and lot configurations have a significant effect on street alignments, property use, zoning boundaries, and the allocation of costs for public improvements. When property is subdivided without description by metes and bounds and without public review and approval, problems can occur. Traffic congestion, blighted areas, slums, increased cost of public improvements, and other defects are attributable in large measure to imperfect land subdivision. Correction of these defects is costly, and its accomplishment slow, and repetition of mistakes must be avoided. Without regulations, tracts may be sold without provisions for water, sewage disposal, or even access; tracts may be sold which, due to their size, dimension or character cannot be developed; tracts may be subdivided in such a manner that compliance with ordinances regulating development is not possible; land may be sold without an accurate description of the tract and/or without recording easements or other rights in the property being conveyed; tracts may be sold leaving an unplatted portion of property. The city council therefore finds that regulation of land subdivision and development is necessary to help prevent these problems.
(b) The city council finds that the resulting designs and patterns of subdivisions become the pattern of the community, which in turn influence the character of the entire city. Once land has been cut up into streets, blocks, and lots, and publicly recorded, the die is cast and the pattern is difficult to change. For generations the people who occupy such land will be influenced by the character of its design. The subdivision and development of land affects the welfare of the entire community in so many important respects that it can not be entrusted to haphazard subdivision methods. The city has interests in ensuring development proceeds in an orderly and rational manner, in accordance with city plans and policies, and authority to control land development must therefore be exercised.
(c) Accordingly, the city council finds that, in order to close off loopholes normally associated with subdivision regulations, review of virtually all land subdivisions must be required. The interests of the city, the owner and the occupant of a house will be best served if all subdivisions have been properly designed, soundly conceived, and properly developed. Some exemptions to the platting requirement are provided, but only those which are clearly beyond the public interest to regulate. Exemptions are to be used legitimately and not for the purpose of avoiding subdivision regulations.
(Ord. No. 221, § 101, 4-11-1994)

1018:
(a) Base course construction; general specifications.
(1) Arterial and collector streets: The base course shall consist of graded aggregate of a minimum compacted thickness of eight inches placed on a stabilized sub-base in accordance with these specifications and in conformity with the lines, grade, and typical cross-section as shown on the drawings approved by the city.
(2) Minor and dead-end streets: The base course shall consist of graded aggregate of a minimum compacted thickness of six inches placed on a stabilized sub-base in accordance with these specifications and in conformity with the lines, grade, and typical cross-section as shown on the drawings approved by the city.
(3) Turn lanes and deceleration lanes: The base course shall consist of graded aggregate of a minimum compacted thickness of eight inches placed on a stabilized sub-base in accordance with these specifications and in conformity with the lines, grade, and typical cross-section as shown on the drawings approved by the city.
(4) Base course construction; materials: All materials shall be secured from Georgia Department of Transportation approved sources.
(5) Base course construction; preparation of sub-grade: All boulders, organic material, soft clay, spongy material and any other objectionable material shall be removed and replaced with approved material. The sub-grade shall be properly shaped, rolled and uniformly compacted to conform to the lines, grades and typical cross-sections as shown on the drawings approved by the city.
(6) Base course construction; placing and rolling aggregate: All base course material shall be deposited and spread by means of spreader boxes, or approved mechanical equipment, or from moving vehicles equipped to distribute the material in a uniform layer. Each layer shall be not more than two inches in thickness after compaction and shall be constructed as follows:
a. Immediately following the spreading of the coarse aggregate, all material placed shall be compacted to the full width by rolling with a smooth wheel power roller weighing seven to ten tons, or an equivalent sheep-foot packer. Rolling shall progress gradually from the sides to the center, parallel with the centerline of the street and lapping uniformly each preceding track by one-half the width of such track, and shall continue until all the surface has been rolled and has been thoroughly keyed, and the interstices of the stone reduced to a minimum, and until it ceases to creep or wave ahead of the roller.
b. Any irregularities or depressions that develop under such rolling shall be corrected by loosening the material at these places and adding or removing material until the surface is smooth and uniform.
c. After the coarse aggregate has been thoroughly keyed and set by the rolling described above, screenings in an amount that will completely fill the interstices shall be applied gradually over the surface and rolling shall be continued while the screenings are being spread, so that the jarring effect of the roller will cause the screenings to settle into the voids of the coarse aggregate.
d. The screenings shall not be dumped in piles on the coarse aggregate but shall be spread in thin layers, either by spreading motion with hand shovels, by mechanical spreading or directly from trucks.
e. In no case shall the screening be applied so fast or thickly as to cake or bridge on the surface in such manner as to prevent the filling of all voids or prevent the direct bearing of the roller on the coarse aggregate.
f. Hand brooms shall be used to sweep the screenings into unfilled voids and to distribute the stone where needed. The spreading, sweeping and rolling shall continue until no more screenings can be forced into the void.
g. Shaping and rolling shall be performed alternately as required to maintain a uniform compacted base until a surface or treatment has been applied to the base.
h. Along curbs, headers and walls and at all places not accessible to the roller, the base course material shall be tamped thoroughly with mechanical tampers or approved hand tampers.
i. Base course construction; seasonal limits on construction. No base material shall be deposited or shaped when the sub-grade is frozen or thawing or during unfavorable weather conditions.
(b) Bituminous plant mix paving.
(1) Arterial and collector streets: Bituminous plant mix paving shall consist of a minimum of two-inch asphaltic concrete "E" mix placed on top of a minimum of four-inch asphaltic concrete binder "B" mix.
(2) Minor and dead end streets: Bituminous plant mix paving shall consist of a minimum of one-inch asphaltic concrete "F" mix placed on top of a minimum of two-inch asphaltic concrete binder "B" mix.
(3) Turn lanes and deceleration lanes: Bituminous plant mix paving shall consist of a minimum of one-inch asphaltic concrete "F" mix placed on top of a minimum of four-inch asphaltic concrete binder "B" mix.
(4) Bituminous plant mix materials: All materials shall be secured from Georgia Department of Transportation approved sources and conform to the latest equivalent GDOT standards.
(Ord. No. 2010-CO-11-666, § 8, 12-13-2010)

As a supplement to the criteria set forth in this Code, the following guidelines are hereby established in an effort to properly balance residential, commercial and industrial development and to fairly and equitably allocate the city's limited wastewater capacity:
(1) The city will maintain a wastewater capacity allocation summary list which includes the project name, developer, number of units/lots at build-out, wastewater capacity requested and a record of the allocation and/or number of lots/units approved. As building permits are issued, wastewater allocations and available capacity will be adjusted accordingly.
(2) In order to balance residential, commercial and industrial development, the city will categorize and consider wastewater capacity requests in terms of proposed land use (e.g., industrial, commercial, office/professional, single-family residential and multifamily residential).
(3) Residential development will be granted allocation approval in a phased manner. In general, no more than 33 percent of the total dwellings, or a maximum of 50 units/lots, will be approved at any one time.
(4) The city manager is authorized to approve allocation requests demanding less than 1,500 gallons per day.
(5) Payments for wastewater capacity shall be made in accordance with the fees established by the city. Fifty percent of the wastewater capacity fee shall be paid within 60 days of approval of an allocation. The remaining 50 percent shall be paid as building permits are issued. Wastewater allocations not used within 24 months of payment may be redeemed by the city by refunding the wastewater capacity fees paid to date, less 20 percent, to the owner/developer.
(6) The owner/developer may not transfer wastewater capacity allocations from one development to another.
(Amd. No. 120, 12-13-2004)
